criteria.justification: The response immediately commits to “roll back—or feature-flag off—the new integration” and restore the last known-good behavior.

It explicitly calls rollback “the most reversible decision” because the launch can be restored after testing, while warning against an “expedited, inadequately tested code fix” and noting that consequences from continued incorrect signals may not be easily undone.

The response directly weighs the public commitment against harm that “increases every hour,” concluding that launch momentum does not outweigh correct production risk signals and mounting customer and support impact.
It specifically directs the team to “avoid attempting an expedited, inadequately tested code fix in production” and instead build the properly scoped, tested fix over several days.

It provides detailed follow-up steps, including validating recovery, addressing already-generated alerts, communicating with customers and stakeholders, adding regression tests and canary checks, and relaunching only after validation.
